body.en: Tense is called the life of the English language. Because without proper knowledge of tense, speaking and writing correct English is impossible, and so is understanding its exact meaning. Although almost every competitive examination has questions on tense, we keep making mistakes again and again. The main reasons are, first, the lack of a clear concept of tense, and second, learning tense through Bengali in the traditional way. Here is an exceptional discussion of all the tenses that are important only for examinations.

body.en: Actions that generally happen or take place in the present in an indefinite way, happen habitually, and happen according to natural law, that is, as eternal truths, are expressed by the Present Indefinite Tense. Note that these actions do not happen at the moment of speaking; that is, they are not connected with any particular time. That is why some people also call this tense the Timeless Tense.

body.en: There are some verbs that are not used in the continuous tense. The common ones among them are: be, have (in the sense of possession), like, love, hate, know, believe, understand, belong, see, hear, want, wish; Linking Verbs — seem, look, taste, appear, feel, smell etc. Note: However, according to position or context these verbs can be used in the continuous tense. For example— Dr. Ali is busy. He is seeing a patient right now. [meeting]

body.en: The Future Indefinite Tense is used to express that some work will happen in the future. body.mix: Ask, advise, command, demand, insist, order, prefer, propose, recommend, request, require, suggest, urge ইত্যাদি Verb-এর পর অথবা necessary, important, imperative, mandatory, obligatory, required, proposed, suggested ইত্যাদি শব্দগুলোর পর যদি that clause আসে তাহলে সেই that clause-এর verb-এর base form হবে, যার সাথে s/es/ies যুক্ত হবে না। এমনকি Main clauseটি Past tense-এ থাকলেও that clause-এর verb-এর সাথে ed/t/ing/would বা অন্য কোনো Modals বসবে না। না-বোধকের ক্ষেত্রে do not/does not/did not বসবে না, শুধু verb-এর পূর্বে not বসবে। Be verb আসলে am/is/are/was/were হবে না, বরং subject-এর পর সরাসরি 'be' বসবে। (উল্লেখ্য, এই নিয়ম Formal American English-এর ক্ষেত্রে প্রযোজ্য। তবে British English এ should + V হবে।)
body.en: After verbs such as ask, advise, command, demand, insist, order, prefer, propose, recommend, request, require, suggest, urge, or after words such as necessary, important, imperative, mandatory, obligatory, required, proposed, suggested, if a that clause comes, the verb of that that clause will be in its base form, with no s/es/ies added. Even if the main clause is in the past tense, no ed/t/ing/would or any other modal will be added to the verb of the that clause. In the negative, do not/does not/did not will not be used; only 'not' will come before the verb. If a be verb comes, it will not be am/is/are/was/were; rather 'be' will come directly after the subject. (Note: this rule applies in Formal American English. In British English, however, it will be should + V.)

body.mix: Present Indefinite Tense বলার সময় ঘটে না, কিন্তু Present Continuous Tense বলার সময় ঘটে। তাই Usually Raju goes to school by car. But Today he is going on foot.
body.en: The Present Indefinite Tense does not happen at the moment of speaking, but the Present Continuous Tense does happen at the moment of speaking. So: Usually Raju goes to school by car. But today he is going on foot.

body.mix: Present Indefinite দ্বারা সময়ের ব্যাপ্তি (Duration) বোঝানো যায় না, কিন্তু Present Perfect বা Perfect Continuous দ্বারা তা বোঝানো যায়। তাই We are friends কিন্তু We have been friends since 1985. তেমনি We live/are living here for 5 years বাক্যটি ভুল কিন্তু We have been living here for 5 years শুদ্ধ।
body.en: Duration of time cannot be expressed by the Present Indefinite, but it can be expressed by the Present Perfect or Perfect Continuous. So: We are friends, but We have been friends since 1985. Similarly, the sentence 'We live/are living here for 5 years' is wrong, but 'We have been living here for 5 years' is correct.

body.mix: 'কোনো কাজ অতীতে শুরু হয়ে এখনও চলছে,'— এরূপ বোঝাতে Present Perfect ও Perfect Continuous উভয়টি ব্যবহার করা যায়। তবে এদের মধ্যে পার্থক্য হলো— যেসব 'Verb' এর Continuous হয় না সেগুলো হয় Present Perfect, বাকিগুলো হয় Perfect Continuous. যেমন— I (be) here for 3 days I have been here for 3 days কিন্তু I (stay) here for 3 days I have been staying here for 3 days. যদিও I have stayed here for 3 days অসম্ভব নয়।
body.en: To express 'an action began in the past and is still continuing', both the Present Perfect and the Perfect Continuous can be used. But the difference between them is— verbs that have no continuous form take the Present Perfect, and the rest take the Perfect Continuous. For example— I (be) here for 3 days: I have been here for 3 days. But: I (stay) here for 3 days: I have been staying here for 3 days. Although 'I have stayed here for 3 days' is not impossible.
